The present DAR arises out of road accident in which one Vishal Majumdar, aged about 19 years, suffered injuries. In terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act, the same is treated as a claim petition. Vishal Majumdar (Dar) vs Akendera Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42569287/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through DD no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road, investigating officer reached the spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was found flipped on the middle of the road. The person injured had been taken to the hospital by then. On reaching the hospital, one of the injured Ganesh Das stated that on 07.11.2021 at 03:00 p.m., he was travelling along with 13 other people in the offending vehicle. After performing religious ritual (idol immersion) near Yamuna River, at Sarai Kale Khan, all the 13 passengers boarded the offending vehicle for returning to Bengali Camp. When the offending tempo reached near Najaf Khan Tomb, Najaf Khan Road, Lodhi Road, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 started driving the vehicle at very high speed recklessly. Despite being cautioned he kept driving the vehicle negligently at high speed, due to which the offending vehicle flipped off, causing injury to its passengers and death of the son of one of the petitioners. Page no. 3 of 04:27:27 25(ss)+0530 2024.10.21 accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP. However, this Court keeping in view the benevolent object of the Act and other relevant factors arising in the case, issued the directions against the Insurance Company to pay the awarded sum to the claimants and then to recover the said sum from the insured in the same proceedings by applying the principle of "pay and recover". 17. Justice R.M. Lodha (as His Lordship then was and later became CJI) speaking for the Bench held in paras 20 and 26 as under: "20. 26. The pendency of consideration of the above questions by a larger Bench does not mean that the course that was followed in Baljit Kaur, (2004) 2 SCC 1 and Challa Upendra Rao, (2004) 8 SCC 517 should not be followed, more so in a peculiar fact situation of this case. In the present case, the accident occurred in 1993. At that time, the claimant was 28 years old. He is now about 48 years. The claimant was a driver on heavy vehicle and due to the accident he has been rendered permanently disabled. He has not been able to get compensation so far due to the stay order passed by this Court. He cannot be compelled to struggle further for GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Vishal Majumdar vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 12 of 25(ss) recovery of the amount. The Insurance Company has already deposited the entire awarded amount pursuant to the order of this Court passed on 1-8-2011 (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Saju P. Paul, SLP No. 20127 of 2011 and the said amount has been invested in a fixed deposit account. The recovery of the amount by the Insurance Company from the owner shall be made by following the procedure as laid down by this Court in Challa Upendra Rao (supra)..." and it was further observed in para "... 22. In view of the foregoing discussion, we are of the view that the direction to United India Insurance Company (respondent No. 3) - they being the insurer of the offending vehicle which was found involved in causing accident due to negligence of its driver needs to be issued directing them (United India Insurance Company-respondent No.3) to first pay the awarded sum to the appellants (claimants) and then to recover the paid awarded sum from the owner of the offending vehicle (Tata Sumo)-respondent No.1 in execution proceedings arising in this very case as per the law laid down in Para 26 of Saju P. Paul's case quoted supra..." As such, as respondent no. 3 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner however, entitled to recovery rights from driver and owner of the offending vehicle. 17. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 GUPTA 04:28:18 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Vishal Majumdar vs. Akendra & 0rs. . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 18. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Vishal Majumdar (Dar) vs Akendera Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42569287/ 8 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.10.21 04:28:22 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Vishal Majumdar vs. Akendra & 0rs. (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 18.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 18.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 18.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 18.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 18.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. Thus, keeping note of the nature of injury suffered by the petitioner and his educational qualifications, it is assumed that he would have been unable to work for atleast 15 days. Thus, he is Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:28:32 Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Vishal Majumdar vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 16 of 25(ss) entitled to compensation of Rs.618X15=9,270/-, towards loss of income on account of the injury. No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability. (v) Loss of income : Rs.9270/- (vi) Cost of artificial limbs (if Not applicable Vishal Majumdar (Dar) vs Akendera Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42569287/ 10 applicable) : (vii) Any other loss / expenditure : Not applicable 2.
texts.facts: In response to the DAR, insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle.
texts.arguments: It is further argued that the insured i.e. respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims.
